description: Build a Spring Boot REST controller with a GET /hello endpoint — by typing every line yourself. No code generation: Teachify guides, you type, Teachify verifies.
learningOutcomes: Explain what @RestController and @GetMapping do in Spring Boot
Explain how Spring maps an HTTP GET to a Java method
Verify a Spring endpoint with curl

quiz.explanation: @RestController marks the class as a web controller whose return values are written directly to the HTTP response body (not resolved to a view).
options: It marks the class as a REST controller whose return values go to the response body
It starts the embedded Tomcat server
quiz.question: What does @RestController do?

quiz.explanation: @GetMapping binds a method to HTTP GET on that path. Without it, Spring would not know when to call the method.
options: It maps HTTP GET /hello to this method
quiz.question: What does @GetMapping("/hello") do?

quiz.explanation: For a @RestController, a String return value becomes the response body. That is why curl shows the greeting.
options: It becomes the HTTP response body
quiz.question: In a @RestController, what happens to the String your method returns?

steps.fileHint: Create it in your controller package, e.g. src/main/java/com/example/demo/HelloController.java.
steps.hintL1: Controllers live in their own file. Create the file first, then we will add the class.
steps.hintL2: Create a file named exactly HelloController.java in your Spring Boot project's controller package.
steps.hintL3: Create the file (empty for now) — in your IDE use New > Java Class, or touch the file. The code comes in later steps.
steps.instruction: Create a new file called HelloController.java in your Spring Boot project.
steps.title: Create HelloController.java
steps.whatToType: Nothing to type yet — just create the empty file in the right package folder.
steps.why: Spring discovers controllers by scanning classes. The file is where your controller class will live.

steps.fileHint: Above the class declaration, after imports and package line.
steps.hintL1: Spring needs to know this class is a web controller. There is an annotation for that.
steps.hintL2: Add the @RestController annotation above your class, and import it from org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.
steps.hintL3: Above the class, type: @RestController — and make sure the class is declared as public class HelloController. You still write the class yourself.
steps.instruction: Declare a public class HelloController and annotate it with @RestController. Add the needed import.
steps.title: Add @RestController
steps.whatToType: An annotation line above the class, plus its import. The class line itself: public class HelloController { ... }.
steps.why: @RestController tells Spring: this class handles HTTP requests, and method return values go straight into the response body.

steps.fileHint: Inside the class, above your handler method.
steps.hintL1: You need to bind one method to HTTP GET on /hello.
steps.hintL2: Use @GetMapping with the path "/hello" above a method. Import GetMapping from the same annotation package.
steps.hintL3: Above your method, type: @GetMapping("/hello") — then ask: which HTTP verb and which path does this bind?
steps.instruction: Add a @GetMapping("/hello") annotation above a handler method.
steps.title: Add @GetMapping("/hello")
steps.whatToType: An annotation with the path "/hello", placed directly above the method that will handle it.
steps.why: Mapping annotations are the routing table. Without one, Spring never calls your method for any URL.

steps.checkDescription: File must declare a public method returning String.
steps.fileHint: Directly under the @GetMapping line, inside the class.
steps.hintL1: The handler must be a method Spring can call. It should return a String.
steps.hintL2: Declare a public method returning String, with no parameters, e.g. public String hello() { ... }.
steps.hintL3: Type: public String hello() { return "Hello from Teachify"; } — then re-read: what does the return value become in the HTTP response?
steps.instruction: Add a public method returning String that returns a short greeting (for example, Hello from Teachify).
steps.title: Add the handler method
steps.whatToType: A public String method. Inside, return a greeting string.
steps.why: The method body is the endpoint logic. In a @RestController, the returned String becomes the response body.

steps.checkDescription: File must return a greeting starting with Hello.
steps.fileHint: Inside your handler method — the return line.
steps.hintL1: Your method should return a greeting. Check the return statement.
steps.hintL2: The return line should return a String starting with Hello.
steps.hintL3: Make sure the line reads like: return "Hello from Teachify"; — then run the app and curl http://localhost:8080/hello yourself to see it.
steps.instruction: Verify your endpoint: run the Spring Boot app yourself, then curl http://localhost:8080/hello and confirm you see your greeting.
steps.title: Run and curl it yourself
steps.whatToType: No new code — run the app with your usual command (./mvnw spring-boot:run or your IDE run), then curl the URL.
steps.why: Code you have not run is a guess. Running + curling proves the mapping, the annotation, and the return value all work together.

title: Build GET /hello with Spring Boot (Java)
